EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (CAI, signed 30 December 2020; ratification pending at EU level)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Company Law, SARL provisions arts. 709-759); Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme (AML/CFT Law), as last substantially amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE Law); Règlement grand-ducal du 14 janvier 2019 relatif au Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; CSSF Regulation N° 12-02 of 14 December 2012; CSSF Circular 18/698 of 23 January 2019; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1675, as amended (high-risk third countries).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (restricted-access national UBO register, 'Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs'): direct access is granted to Luxembourg competent authorities (FIU, CSSF, tax administration, judicial authorities); obliged entities (credit institutions, notaries, lawyers, TCSPs) may consult in the course of customer due diligence; natural or legal persons demonstrating a legitimate interest may apply for extract access; general public access has been suspended following the Court of Justice of the European Union judgment of 22 November 2022, Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 (WM and Sovim SA).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport/ID issuing authority or notary public in the document origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961); consular legalization if the origin state is not a Contracting Party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each shareholder and manager (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or licensed credit institution in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, current excerpt from the commercial register, and certificate of good standing for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies register of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and KYC/AML attestation issued by the existing banking relationship of each ultimate beneficial owner and corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution maintaining the existing relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Curriculum vitae and signed source-of-wealth / source-of-funds statement for each ultimate beneficial owner
Power of Attorney appointing the Luxembourg incorporation agent / law firm (if acting through an authorized representative)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholder(s) and authorized signature holder(s)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed declaration of non-condemnation for criminal offences and absence of insolvency, bankruptcy or disqualification proceedings for each proposed manager (gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille, or signature certified before the Luxembourg notary at incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP identification, verification and enhanced due diligence per art. 3(7) and art. 5 of the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF Circular 18/698 (Chapter 3.2.2). Mandatory pre-acceptance screening against: (i) consolidated EU financial sanctions lists under EU Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and EU Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) OFAC SDN/Non-SDN and sectoral sanctions lists given USD payment rails and US counterparties; (iv) domestic Luxembourg FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) indicators and criminal-records verification for managers; and (v) FATF public statements and the EU high-risk third-country list under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1675, as amended. Continuous watchlist monitoring and re-screening at every trigger event is mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — official electronic portal: https://www.lbr.lu; name reservation and RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) filings are executed through the LBR e-filing platform, with notary-mediated clearance performed via the notarial 'e-Company' workflow at incorporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filings with the RCS must be in one of the administrative languages of Luxembourg (French, German, or Luxembourgish); articles of association are conventionally drafted in French, and if executed in English a certified French version must accompany the registration filing. The company name may employ Latin-alphabet characters of any EU language; non-Latin scripts require a Latin-alphabet transliteration recorded in the RCS and in the articles of association. The legal form designation 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' must be identifiable in the notarial deed.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the LBR/RCS, the applicant or its notary shall: (1) obtain the written refusal reasons through the LBR registry service or notary; (2) file a new, distinct name reservation request immediately; (3) if the rejection is contested on grounds of confusing similarity, trademark priority, or public policy, lodge a formal 'recours gracieux' (administrative appeal) with the Minister of Justice within one month of notification, and alternatively institute proceedings before the Tribunal Administratif (Administrative Tribunal) within three months of the contested decision; (4) where the conflict arises from a third-party prior right, seek and file a written letter of consent from the prior right holder to permit registration; (5) in time-sensitive incorporations, reserve an alternative compliant name while pursuing the appeal in parallel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for incorporation and RCS registration, provided the registered office (siège social) is a fixed physical address in Luxembourg at which service of process can be effected. For an AI video-generation SaaS company (ISIC 6201, standard low-risk AML tier, no statutory license), a virtual office with mail handling, domiciliation and administrative support is permissible at formation; however, ongoing economic substance will be scrutinized by the Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes) for tax-residence, VAT and treaty-benefit purposes, and by the CSSF in its oversight of the TCSP service provider.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (estimated 25-30% probability of an unannounced physical on-site verification within the first 24 months) for a virtual-office SARL engaged in AI SaaS activities with non-resident shareholders; probability rises to 40-50% if the company claims the Luxembourg IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), applies for VAT refunds, or executes cross-border intercompany transactions requiring transfer-pricing documentation; inspections may be conducted by the tax administration in coordination with the CSSF and the FIU.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 1, 180 to 201 for SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and Company Accounts; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), in coordination with the Ministry of Justice and the House of Entrepreneurship.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Charter of incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) executed by notarial deed; followed by electronic filing with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL minimum share capital is EUR 12,000 (approx. USD 13,200); must be fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in kind; beneficial owner declarations and bank attestation of payment required; no escrow account required unless an in-kind contribution is made.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation deed of the SARL is approved and the statutory capital of EUR 12,000 is deemed fully subscribed and paid up. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the address stated in the deed and that this address be registered with the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED, that the manager(s) named in the articles are appointed and authorised to represent the company. RESOLVED, that the first financial year ends on December 31. RESOLVED, that the initial compliance filings, VAT registration and social security registration are delegated to the appointed professional.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and notarize the incorporation charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) in coordination with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to draft the notarial deed of incorporation (statuts). The charter must include the SARL's corporate name, legal form, registered office address, corporate object (including software development and AIGC video synthesis), share capital, share classes, number of shares, appointment of managers, and winding-up provisions. All founder decisions must be captured in a notarized protocol. The notary will verify identity, legal capacity, and beneficial ownership details. Execute the deed before the notary and obtain certified copies.
required_dossiers: Original and copy of passport (or ID card) of each founder
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within 3 months)
Certificate of criminal good conduct from country of residence (if required by notary)
Bank certificate or attestation confirming payment and blocking of the fully paid-up share capital on a Luxembourg bank account
Draft articles of association in French or Luxembourgish
Beneficial owner declaration form (form 3 for the RCS beneficial owner register)
Power of attorney if a founder is represented
Business plan and details of registered office address if supplied by a professional service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects missing capital attestation or defects in the deed, the founders shall provide the correct bank certificate or amend the deed. If the notary refuses to pass the deed, resubmit corrected documents within 15 days. Rejection from the RCS is cured by filing a formal rectification and paying the administrative resubmission fee (EUR 30).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (electronic filing via lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, file the notarial deed electronically with the RCS using the online platform lbr.lu. Attach the notarised charter, the appointed manager's acceptance, and the beneficial owner register form. Pay the registration fee online via credit card or bank transfer. The registration is completed after the RCS checks the legality and due publication of the deed in the electronic compendium of companies (Recueil électronique des sociétés).
required_dossiers: Notarised incorporation deed (statuts)
Manager acceptance letter and identity documents
Beneficial owner register form (form 3)
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or sublease, or professional domiciliation agreement)
Bank capital payment attestation
Completed RCS electronic filing form (form A or B as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (demande de complément), the notary or authorized agent must submit the missing piece within one month. If case is temporarily suspended, reply with all missing details. Rejection can be appealed to the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 2 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for corporate income tax, VAT and social security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the RCS registration number (and VAT number request), file the mandatory tax registration forms. With the RCS registration extract, register with the ACD for income tax and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal). Register with the AEDT for VAT (TVA) using the normal rate of 17% (standard export of software services is taxable in the destination country; intra-community supplies fall under reverse charge). Register the manager and any employees with the CCSS for social security.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (certificat d'immatriculation)
Articles of association
VAT registration form (form 102) and identification form
Managers' details and civil status certificate
Expected turnover and place of supply statement
Bank ownership certificate (RIB)
Social security registration form for the manager (so-called 'statut du dirigeant' form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT queries classification of services, provide a detailed description of the AI video generation SaaS platform and the place of taxation (B2B reverse charge). For CCSS vectors, re-submit the manager contract. Tax registrations may be appealed by filing a claim with the tax administration within 3 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt corporate governance and open the Luxembourg bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank (e.g. BIL, BCEE, Intesa Sanpaolo) and the company's managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Organize the first board meeting to adopt the first board resolution, decide on banking arrangements, and approve the opening of a corporate bank account. Provide the bank with the RCS extract, notarized articles, manager ID, and statement of account purpose. For the AI avatar video SaaS license, the bank may require a business plan and proof of low AML risk. Once the account is opened, ensure the share capital remains blocked for the duration of the notary process, and transfer it into the operational account after registration.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of incorporation
Notarized articles of association
First board resolution approving bank account and officer appointments
Identity and proof of address of the manager and beneficial owners
Business plan and AML low-risk justification
Source of funds statement for share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank asks for additional beneficial ownership declaration, provide the updated RCS register extract. If account opening is refused, appeal to the bank's compliance officer or select a different bank. For persistent refusal due to the AIGC scope, provide the low-risk classification and a letter explaining no high-risk payment activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the census and statistical declaration if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Statec (National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies of Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of the RCS registration, complete the statistical census (déclaration d'activité) online. The declaration is mandatory for all companies on the national register. For a SaaS business, describe the primary activity as 'publishing of other software' (NACE 62.01 / ISIC 6201). This step is purely statistical and done automatically with RCS data for most companies; an online confirmation is sufficient.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number
Company seat address
Business classification code (ISIC 6201 / NACE 62.01)
Manager's name and nationality
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the online form is rejected, verify the NACE code and re-submit. No adverse remedy needed, as the RCS may auto-validate the statistical filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Directorate General for Industry and New Technologies
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific industrial operating license required for software publishing (ISIC 6201)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Agency (Administration de l'environnement, AEV)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is a purely digital software service with no physical production facility, no wastewater discharge, no air emissions and no hazardous waste generation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – zero direct emissions, zero industrial discharge; the company must comply with general waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) Directive (2012/19/EU) and the RoHS Directive for any IT hardware; if using internal servers, comply with Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ecodesign) and the Energy Efficiency Directive. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are zero because no paint/coating processes exist.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office workspace must comply with Luxembourg fire safety and OSH standards (Ministry of Labour). A fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) may be required if the rented premises are open to the public, but for a standard SaaS office a self-assessment and landlord attestation are sufficient. Staff workstations must meet the Directive 90/270/EEC on display screen equipment. For any AI video render farm hardware, obtain the electricity safety certificate and structural load assessment from the building's civil engineer if server racks are installed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties, and excise. Official e-filing portal: MyGuichet.lu (centralized administrative portal); VAT and corporate tax returns are submitted via the ACD's eTVA module and MyGuichet.lu with national identification number authentication.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned SARL obtains its Luxembourg tax identity as follows: (1) Execute deed of incorporation before a Luxembourg notary and deposit statutory capital (minimum EUR 12,000; EUR 12,000 paid-in for SARL); (2) Notary registers the company with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) within one month, obtaining the RCS registration number (B number) and the national identification number; (3) The RCS automatically transmits registration data to the ACD and AEDT, which issue the direct tax number and the VAT number in the format LU + 8 digits; (4) For direct VAT registration by a non-resident entity without RCS registration, file form 5200 with the AEDT via MyGuichel.lu, appoint a fiscal representative if no permanent establishment and no EU-established person, and provide articles of association, proof of foreign registration, and intended activity description; (5) Apply for a separate intra-Community operator status (in-scope of the same VAT number) by declaring prospective intra-EEA distance sales and services to the AEDT; the same VAT number serves for both domestic and intra-Community purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply the check-the-box regime; the SARL is a taxable entity subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax. Available elective regimes include: (a) group integration under Article 164bis L.I.R. (fiscal unity for 95% or more of share capital and voting rights); (b) VAT grouping election (assujettis uniques) under Article 62 of the VAT law allowing a single taxable person for related entities; (c) the IP box regime (80% exemption and 0% effective tax on qualifying IP income) requires an election and R&D nexus tracking; (d) participation exemption (parent-subsidiary) election for substantial shareholdings (>=10% or EUR 1.2M acquisition cost, held >=12 months); (e) advance tax agreement (tax ruling) procedure before the ACD for economic substance, transfer pricing, and hybrid mismatch treatment; ATAD hybrid mismatch rules apply and no unilateral hybrid election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual business turnover for locally established taxable persons (franchise exemption under Article 57 VAT law); no mandatory registration threshold below EUR 35,000 if the business is exclusively outside the scope of VAT. Non-resident taxable persons making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register immediately from the first euro. For intra-Community distance sales and cross-border digital B2C services, the EU distance sales threshold (EUR 10,000) applies, but the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme must be used for OSS-registered businesses.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: As of the effective date, Luxembourg does not mandate universal B2B e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance. Mandatory e-invoicing applies solely to public-sector invoices under the EN 16931 / PEPPOL format (EU Directive 2014/55/EU). For AI avatar SaaS cross-border sales, the taxpayer must issue technically compliant electronic invoices in EU standard format for intra-EU B2B supplies (reverse charge), submit recapitulative statements (deferred until the 10th of the following month) via eTVA/MyGuichet.lu, and retain real-time transaction log access for audit. The EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) framework will require standardized e-invoicing and digital transaction reporting for intra-EU B2B supplies by 2030 (targeted 2027-2028); actionable compliance readiness is required on that horizon.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods dispatched to a destination outside the EU: zero-rating under Article 56 of the Luxembourg VAT law applies if physical removal from Luxembourg/EEA is evidenced by transport documents and the goods leave the EU within 90 days of dispatch. For software/AI video services: B2B exports to customers outside the EU are outside the territorial scope of Luxembourg VAT under the place-of-supply rule where the customer is established; no zero-rating claim is required but the supplier must obtain the foreign customer's B2B evidence and business status. B2C digital services sold to non-EU consumers are treated as performed outside the EU and therefore outside Luxembourg VAT. For intra-EU B2B SaaS supplies, zero-rating is replaced by reverse charge with a valid EU VAT number and by submitting a recapitulative statement; failure to satisfy the documentary threshold converts the supply to a domestic taxable transaction at 16%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/EX1 or customs-stamped export certificate)
Bill of Lading (ocean), CMR (road), or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical escape from the EU
Commercial invoice (with reference to the 0% rate and place-of-supply rule)
Proof of payment: inward remittance certificate (SWIFT or bank confirmation), together with contract and the foreign customer's VAT registration/identification evidence
For digital SaaS exports: signed client agreement, customer self-declaration of non-EU establishment, and technical license/hosting/IP transfer documentation showing the place of beneficial usage
Intra-EU supplies: recapitulative statement (ESL) with destination customer VAT numbers and evidence of reverse-charge notification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT conducts documentary audits, clawing back erroneously zero-rated output VAT (16% plus late-payment interest at monthly statutory rates, currently 0.8% per month) if export evidence is absent or deficient. Negligent or fraudulent claims attract a pecuniary fine of EUR 250 to EUR 10,000 per offense, a fine representing up to three times the evaded tax, and criminal liability (imprisonment up to five years) under Articles 396 et seq. of the General Tax Law and Article 65 of the VAT law. For SaaS/digital exports, a retroactive reclassification of zero-rated B2C sales to the Luxembourg or recipient-state rate may also trigger OSS obligations and additional penalties; the clawback period extends five years from the end of the taxable year in ordinary cases, and ten years in cases of proven fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (Central Bank of Luxembourg, BCL), acting in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking supervision and conduct-of-business matters
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full currency convertibility under EU free movement of capital rules (TFEU Article 63). There is no legal distinction between current and capital account transactions for exchange control purposes. Profit remittances and distributions may flow freely to resident and non-resident shareholders, subject only to corporate law solvency tests, applicable dividend withholding taxes, and standard AML/KYC verification by the paying bank. No prior exchange-control authorization is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg does not impose any statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or requirement to repatriate export proceeds into EUR. Exporters may retain foreign currency balances in Luxembourg bank accounts. Cross-border payments and external positions remain subject solely to BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting as requested by the reporting bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for offshore digital EMI accounts; Medium for EU-licensed electronic money institutions passporting into Luxembourg under the Payment Services Directive 2 (PSD2). Offshore EMIs without a Luxembourg or EU licence are not acceptable treasury counterparties for capital escrow, account freezing certificates, or corporate settlement accounts. Payment facilitation via Stripe and Paddle is commercially viable for card and online collection, but the SARL's primary treasury and reserved capital accounts must be held at a licensed bank in Luxembourg or an EU/EEA credit institution passporting into Luxembourg.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Pure remote account opening is generally not available for the initial corporate account at Luxembourg banks. At least one managing director, statutory manager, or authorised signatory must appear physically at the chosen Luxembourg bank for the KYC interview and signature verification. Some banks permit video interviews for existing professional clients, but for a newly formed SARL a physical presence meeting is the prevailing industry expectation. Documentary originals or certified copies of the articles of association, notarial deed, trade register extract, and UBO register excerpt are required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Online-only business model with global subscription revenue settled through Stripe and Paddle and no physical storefront or traditional sales presence in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the bank with a board-approved business plan, product documentation, linked company website and live AI-video platform, merchant agreements with Stripe and Paddle, PCI DSS compliance attestation, historical or projected settlement statements, customer segment breakdown, AI content moderation policy, and a clear explanation of the AIGC SaaS revenue flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value or high-volume cross-border receipts originating from a broad and partially non-EU client base, increasing sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening complexity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply an active jurisdiction list for clients, OFAC/EU sanctions and adverse-media screening results, UBO and counterparty KYC files for material business clients, export control and data-transfer documentation for non-EU markets, cybersecurity and anti-fraud framework, and a legal opinion or compliance manual demonstrating that the revenue comes from permissible software services only.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible asset concentration, software IP ownership, and related-party licensing or royalty flows between the Luxembourg SARL and other group entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a documented IP ownership register for the avatar-generation software and video-synthesis algorithms, registered trademark and patent certificates, software escrow agreement, intercompany licence and service agreements, transfer pricing documentation aligned with OECD and Luxembourg arm's-length principles, and audited or management financial statements proving commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Leveraged use of a registered office, domiciliation provider, or corporate-services package creating low-physical-substance exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the lease or sub-lease agreement for the registered office, physical substance evidence such as workstations or local administrative facilities, employment contracts or service contracts for Luxembourg-based staff and officers, minutes of board and shareholder meetings held in Luxembourg, and the domiciliation provider's engagement letter together with a CSSF-compliant substance explanation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial SARL capital, the subscribing shareholder must transfer cash in EUR to the Luxembourg bank's capital escrow or ordinary blocked account before or immediately after notarisation of the articles of association. Use SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA inbound wires or SEPA Credit Transfer for EU-origin payments. The payment purpose and bank reference must clearly state 'Opération en capital / Capital contribution' and the SARL corporate name and registered corporate number. The receiving bank applies the BCL Balance of Payments functional classification 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital.' Verification evidence includes the notarial deed of incorporation, capital subscription form, bank account blocking certificate, shareholder payment instruction from the originating bank, KYC documentation for the ultimate beneficial owner, and confirmation that the minimum statutory capital of €12,000 is fully paid and available free of encumbrance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border trade and SaaS operational disbursements, Luxembourg treasury operations should use SEPA Credit Transfers for EU suppliers and SWIFT MT103 for non-EU payments in foreign currency or where the receiving bank is outside the SEPA zone. Commercial Letters of Credit are appropriate only for physical goods scenarios; for software, royalty, licence, cloud-infrastructure, and subcontractor payments, standard telegraphic transfers with correct corporate purpose codes are the preferred rail. High-value EUR settlements are cleared through TARGET2, with SWIFT for message routing. For all outbound disbursements the bank will apply BCL balance-of-payments reporting classifications and may require underlying agreements such as supplier contracts, invoices, licence agreements, and board-approved disbursement minutes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign exchange spot contracts for immediate conversion of receivables and disbursements
Outright EUR/USD or EUR/GBP forward contracts, with maturities aligned to invoicing and collection cycles, for hedging commercial currency exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies where local delivery is restricted, provided the counterparty bank accepts the corporate's underlying commercial exposure
Cross-currency swaps for larger or longer-dated asset and liability mismatches, subject to bank credit limits and board-approved treasury policy
European-style exchange-traded or OTC options used exclusively to hedge costs and revenues, not for speculative open positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial-owner particulars under the Luxembourg RBE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the annual anniversary of the date of RBE registration; for most entities this falls once per year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Written reminder followed by administrative fine of up to EUR 25,000; directors may also incur criminal fines and imprisonment; continued breach may be reported to AML authorities and the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts of the SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end the filing is due by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS may apply to the commercial court for an injunction; directors risk coercive fines and court-sanctioned publication of non-compliance; persistent default can lead to administrative strike-off of the SARL from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard deadline for a calendar-year company is 30 June of the following year; an extension to 30 November is available upon request and is routinely granted for e-filings.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ACD may issue an estimated assessment; late payment gives rise to statutory late interest and a default surcharge; failure after notice can result in enforcement proceedings and criminal penalty exposure for directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL is exempt from the statutory audit as a small undertaking unless it exceeds more than one of: total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average 50 employees during the financial year. An audit is mandatory if the SARL is not small, is part of a consolidated group exceeding audit thresholds, has 250+ employees, or is otherwise designated as a public-interest entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts are prepared under Luxembourg GAAP (Luxembourg accounting law implementing Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU is available for voluntary adoption and required for listed/public-interest entities in consolidated filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, the SARL must access the RBE portal and confirm that its beneficial-owner record remains accurate within one month after the annual anniversary of RBE registration. Any share transfer that changes direct or indirect ownership must be reported as an update before the annual confirmation; if no change has occurred, the annual confirmation simply republishes the last filed data.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 2,800 per year for a standard SARL including registered office, registered-agent and annual filing handling services in Luxembourg.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - USD 9,500 for an audit of a small or medium-size Luxembourg SARL, excluding pass-through expenses and tax-advisory services.
